analysis:
Examined Gemma4TensorParallelPagedSession.swift and Gemma4TensorParallelPlan.swift in full (head text and patch). The Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.swift unit (e7767f1afa0147d1:0) had only metadata and a truncated patch excerpt, so its body was not reviewed. That is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.

Paged session: it validates frontier, range, vocabulary bounds, page reservation and batch size (1...8, distinct sessions of one model). It retires state on failure and checks the host drains. No plaintext handling, network or keying logic was added. Failure paths use ProbeError and retire(failed:), so I see no information disclosure or fail-open regression.

Plan: it parses the artifact config.json and rejects untied heads, a non-MoE model, shared KV, unknown layer kinds and non-affine or non-4/8-bit quantization. Quantization overrides must name a known module, a layer in range, and the default group size. It checks that head, vocabulary, group and word splits are whole. cut() throws on vision and unknown tensors, so unexpected weights are not silently loaded. localShape checks that cuts stay within the tensor and land on group and word boundaries. This is mostly input validation and fails closed. One minor point: expectedShape does not check that the key's layer index is canonical, whereas cut() does (String(layer) == ...). That is not exploitable on its own.

Prefix cache (T-041, TB-007): the changed prefix file's own description says it uses the pipeline's scoped keys (ClusterWorkerPrefixCache.scope, tenant partition) and an encrypted SSD tier. It claims boundaries are voted over a sealed sum and written only after clean retirement on both ranks. I could not verify this from the supplied excerpt. The next pass should confirm three things: tenant and cacheSalt scoping, SSD tier encryption and HMAC-keyed names, and the TTL, so that this tier does not widen the T-041 at-rest or cross-tenant surface. The same pass should confirm that the zero-padded shared-middle-group design in the plan is covered by the arithmetic-agreement check between ranks, and that peer ranks cannot supply mismatched plans.
